speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your symptoms in detail, specifically when the vertigo started, if it is constant or episodic, and whether you experience hearing loss, tinnitus, or nausea.

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

The history of sudden onset lasting only 3 minutes while in bed, with complete resolution to baseline, is classic for BPPV. Do you notice any specific head movements, such as looking up or rolling over in bed, that trigger these episodes?
